text:
Directives of the Tribal Council are based upon presentation and approval of resolutions. Such resolutions can be presented after approval of an Executive Committee.
The Constitution allows for establishment and election of committees to perform various functions or tasks assigned to them by the Tribal Council. Generally, these committees are charged with the responsibility of making reports and recommendations to the Tribal Council. The degree of authority extended to these committees by the Tribal Council to act on behalf of the tribe has varied over time and with particular issues. Furthermore, committees are not always permanent; some are created to address a specific need at a particular period of time. A sample of committees existant in 1974 are: Education, Enrollment, Housing, Industrial Development, Law and Order, Land Resources, Minerals, Recreation, Water Resources, Executive, Social, Economics and Culture.
Committee members are elected by the Tribal Council at large or in the reservation districts, depending upon the responsibilities and duties assigned to the committees by Council resolutions. The Tribal Council is considered the official voice of the Crow Tribe, although its wishes and desires are often expressed through the officers and committees.
